_what: Human-verified ground truth for audio-only (scriptless) QC. Every entry was confirmed by a person LISTENING to the audio, not derived from any tool output. This file exists because that knowledge previously lived only in commit messages and chat, which is how two changes shipped on plausible reasoning and had to be reverted (local-drift 982485c, and the relative-only music gate that killed a verified drop).
_how_to_use: python -m tests.score_ear_truth <report.json> <case-id>. A change is only an improvement if verified_missing recall does not fall AND false_flag count does not rise. Flag COUNTS alone are noise: identical inputs have produced 28-48 transcript lines and, before the VAD-window change, two identical EP41 runs shared 1 of 8 flags.
_provenance: Verdicts given by the studio-side user (pmo@rian.io) in Audacity, 2026-07-30 and 2026-08-03, against drift-aligned window pairs. tolerance_s is how close a flag must land to count as a hit.

poa-ep12.description: POA (Paulo, O Apostolo) EP12, Portuguese original video vs the delivered English DIALOGUE_EN track. FIRST ground truth found by the tool in a delivery the studio had NOT yet QC-ed, ear-verified by the user 2026-08-06 and corroborated by the cached Scribe transcripts of both sides. Engine: Scribe. The run produced 33 MISSING flags, of which 18 were the untranslated opening SONG (00:16-01:22) - a systematic false-positive class, see note_expected.

verified_missing.note: 'Nao e possivel, seu charlatao.' - user ear-verified MISSING 2026-08-06; the dub transcript jumps 360.7-361.8 'and the sky above' straight to 366.1 'You know what, Barnabas?', a 4.3 s hole exactly where the original speaks. FLAGGED by the tool (low confidence). WALLA SUBSTITUTION (user + waveform, 2026-08-06): the original line is QUIET, and the dub does not leave a hole - it carries continuous crowd ambience there (mean -25.5 dB, peak -21.7 dB, dynamic range only 15 dB, i.e. no inter-word silences), versus real dub speech either side of it which swings from -120 dB to -25 dB. So the specific line was never dubbed and the gap is covered by generic walla. [end corrected 363.5 -> 363.48: the earlier value was ESTIMATED, not read from the report; measured duration is 1.58s]

Crowd heckles 'Mentira.' / 'Mentiroso total.' / 'Voces sao mentirosos.' - user heard it as missing (unsure, noisy section); transcripts corroborate: the dub goes from 'Don't be like them' (ends 1215.8) to one 1216.0-1221.5 segment 'He, he's proof that we're not fooling anyone', with no heckle content at all. FLAGGED by the tool at 1216.62 (MEDIUM confidence - the run's only medium-tier true positive). Same WALLA SUBSTITUTION signature: dub mean -24.1 dB with only 10.5 dB of dynamic range across the window - continuous crowd wash, not dialogue. [end corrected 1218.6 -> 1217.23: the earlier value was ESTIMATED, not read from the report; measured duration is 0.93s]

'O que?' - present

poa-ep12.note_expected: Recall must include BOTH verified_missing entries; the tool caught both on 2026-08-06 (Scribe). Known false-positive classes on this episode: the 00:16-01:22 opening song (18 flags - songs stay untranslated by design) and short interjections that are present but quiet. Of the 9 flags ear-checked, 2 were real, 6 present, 1 ambiguous.
poa-ep12.walla_substitution_note: BOTH true positives on this episode share one pattern: the dub replaces an un-dubbed crowd/reaction line with generic ambience rather than leaving silence. Two consequences. (1) DETECTION RISK: walla sits at speech-like levels (-24 to -25 dB), so if Silero ever classifies it as speech the acoustic tie-breaker suppresses the flag as 'dub speaks here'. It did not here (slot coverage 0.07 and 0.0), but that is the near-miss to watch - it is the most likely source of a future false NEGATIVE on crowd scenes. (2) OPPORTUNITY: 'original has a line, dub has continuous low-dynamic-range energy and no transcript' is a distinctive, checkable signature - a candidate finding type of its own ('covered by ambience' vs 'silent hole') that would raise precision rather than lower it.
poa-ep12.confidence_tier_note: CORRECTION (2026-08-06): an earlier note claimed medium-confidence flags were '3/3 true positives'. That was selective counting — EP12's own song block contained medium flags (all false), and EP9 @2558.6 is a medium+ambience FALSE positive. Across everything ear-checked so far the honest tally is: MEDIUM ~ mixed; the strongest single predictor is the dub-fill label SILENCE (4/4 real: EP10 x3, EP11 x1), while AMBIENCE is 2/3 (EP12 x2 real, EP9 x1 false). Small samples — do not over-fit.

poa-ep10.note_expected: CORRECTED 2026-08-06: the 14:31-14:56 cluster was first recorded as three dropped dialogue lines on the strength of an ear-check (Portuguese present, English silent). That hearing was right but the INTERPRETATION was wrong — all three lyrics recur verbatim inside the closing-song block at 38:16-38:36, so it is a mid-episode reprise of the same untranslated song. Block grouping missed it because the three lines sit ~16 s and ~9 s apart (over the 10 s window) and number only 3 (under the 4-line minimum). PROPOSED RULE: a missing line whose text also appears inside a detected song block is the same song — tag it to that block instead of reporting it as dialogue. Would have removed all three automatically.

poa-ep22.invalidated_note: RETRACTED 2026-08-07. This episode was QC'd from a SUMMED speaker folder, and that folder is not a timeline set: of its 45 tracks, 34 have different lengths (148 s to 3376 s) and the short ones carry BWF TimeReference = 0, so nothing records where they belong. The summing code stacked every track from 00:00, which moves those characters' dialogue to the top of the episode and leaves their true slots silent — indistinguishable from a dropped line. The two drops recorded here (1052.92, 1055.96) were ear-verified AND transcript-verified, but BOTH used that fabricated dub, so neither is trustworthy. The user spotted it from a clip that was silent in a way that felt wrong. Re-verify against a real mixed dub before restoring. EP21 (39 tracks, all 444 MB) and EP23 (48 tracks, all 343 MB) are uniform full-length sets and remain valid.

sung_detector_result.verdict: The critical question — is real dialogue being taken off the timeline — came back clean: 0 of 16. Errors run in the safe direction (2 songs missed, i.e. under-suppression). Suppression is safe at this scale.

_measurement_rule: Durations/ends in verified_missing MUST be copied from the run's report.json, never estimated. An estimated set of ends made a duration-based false-flag rule look perfect in validation while it actually demoted a verified drop (2026-08-07).

poa-show.verified: 2026-08-10, by ear, on EP04 and EP11 opening themes
poa-show.what_was_heard: The English delivery's FULL STEREO MIX carries the original PORTUGUESE vocal through the theme song. The song is retained untranslated, not re-sung in English.
poa-show.why_it_matters: A song line can never be a real finding, so every flag inside a song region is noise. It also explains a result that would otherwise mislead: comparing EP11 against the full stereo mix removed 28 of 31 song-region flags, which looks like 'the song was dubbed and lives in the music stem'. It is not — the original Portuguese audio is sitting in the English mix, so it matched ITSELF. Do not switch the dub source to the full mix on the strength of that number; it also took ordinary-dialogue false flags from 6 to 11.
poa-show.mechanism: Demucs' vocals stem contains SINGING by definition, so separating the original hands us a clean a cappella of the theme (measured -31.5 dBFS through EP11's opening song, vs -30.9 during dialogue). The dub side is a dialogue-only delivery which cannot contain a song vocal (-180 dBFS, digital silence). Nothing in the pipeline asks whether a line was sung or spoken.
poa-show.chosen_fix: (accompaniment - vocals) dB per line, from the two stems already cached. Sung lines median +1.7 dB, spoken lines median -12.3 dB over 8 episodes / 327 flags. At a 0 dB threshold: 72% of song lines caught, 9.8% of dialogue mislabelled, and all four ear-verified real drops safely below (closest -2.0 dB).
